Recently, an increasing number of users have complained that their Macs experience a spinning beach wheel when running macOS 26.5, with some saying their trackpad completely stops responding for several seconds.

Activity Monitor usually shows three 'culprits', and there now appears to be a reliable solution...

I mentioned this issue last month, speculating at the time that it might be caused by the photo scanning feature of Apple Intelligence. When checking Activity Monitor, you typically see one, two, or three processes taking up extremely high CPU usage.

Macworld's Michael Simon has also fallen victim to this.

He tried various methods without success, and eventually found an effective solution: delete the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. Doing so of course means the Mac has to rebuild the Spotlight index, but he said the issue did not recur after two weeks. My own test time was less than a day, but so far I have not encountered the same problem either.

If you don't mind waiting for Spotlight data to be rebuilt, you can follow these steps to delete the relevant data:

  • Open a Finder window
  • From the 'Go' menu, select 'Go to Folder...'
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Press CMD-A to select all, then right-click any item and choose 'Move to Trash'
  • Right-click the Trash icon and select 'Empty Trash'
  • Click Confirm in the pop-up confirmation prompt

If you've been plagued by this issue, feel free to let me know in the comments whether this method works for you too.
